findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is removed with local-only API
findings.body: After this change RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can return a credential from getFederatedCredentialsStream, but when allCodesUsed is true the code still calls credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). That API removes a locally stored credential, not a credential owned by a user-storage provider, and the federated model's id may be null or synthetic. The exhausted federated credential therefore remains in user storage while the user is only given the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action; if that action is not completed, the stale exhausted credential remains and subsequent login can again select it. Federated exhaustion needs disableCredentialType/removal through the federated updater rather than removeStoredCredentialById.

findings.title: Login bean crashes when federated recovery credential is absent, type-only, or exhausted
findings.body: The bean now obtains the credential through RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential and immediately calls credentialModelOpt.get(), RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel on it, and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). For a local user configuredFor was previously backed by the same stored stream that the bean read, but a federated provider can report isConfiguredFor/supportsCredentialType while its getCredentials returns no recovery model, a type-only model without local-format credentialData, or a model whose codes are all used. Any of those cases throws NoSuchElementException or a credential-data parsing RuntimeException while rendering the login form, producing a server error instead of a usable challenge or required-action flow.

findings.title: Recovery-code user label is dropped when creating the credential through updateCredential
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential builds the UserCredentialModel only from credentialModel.getType() and the JSON codes, without transferring credentialModel.getUserLabel() (the device/label) or the generation time. The previous required-action code called createCredential with the full RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel built from generatedCodes, generatedAt and generatedUserLabel, preserving the label for local storage. Now the updateCredential path used for user storage, and for local storage when the recovery provider handles updateCredential, receives no label, so the created recovery-code credential loses the user-provided label that is shown for credential management.

findings.title: Federated recovery codes in the test storage are reusable and one-time use is not tested
findings.body: The new federated isValid implementation returns true if any stored raw code equals the input, without removing or marking that code as used, and getCredentials rebuilds every stored code as unused via createFromValues. Consequently the new integration test, which logs in only once with code index 0, runs with indefinitely replayable recovery codes and can never exercise the authenticator's allCodesUsed cleanup/required-action branch for federated users. The test should consume/mark the used code in the storage double and assert that reusing the same code fails and that the next login requests the next code.

findings.title: Federated getCredentials discards the stored recovery credential id
findings.body: updateCredential stores the recovery credential with an id generated at line 195, but getCredentials creates a fresh RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues from the raw codes and never copies myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() onto the returned model, unlike the OTP branch which returns the stored credential with its id. Callers that use the federated credential id, such as deletion from account credential management and the authenticator's cleanup of exhausted codes, therefore receive a null or unrelated id and cannot address the credential actually stored in the user storage, making those federated flows untestable/incorrect with this storage double.
